name: Bolivia
summary: Red, yellow and green horizontal bands. Adopted in 1851, the civil flag is plain, and the state flag adds the coat of arms. Since 2009 the Wiphala, a square flag of indigenous Andean peoples, has also been an official national symbol.
origin: After independence in 1825, Bolivia used several flags of green and red, then red, yellow and green. President Manuel Isidoro Belzu set the current order on 31 October 1851.
The 2009 Constitution, under President Evo Morales, made the Wiphala, a patchwork of seven colours in diagonal squares, a symbol of the state alongside the tricolour.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The bravery of the Bolivian soldiers and the blood shed for the republic.

facts: The Wiphala has been a co-official national symbol since 2009.
Bolivia celebrates Flag Day on 17 August.
Ghana and Lithuania use the same three colours in different orders; Ghana adds a black star.
clues: Red, yellow and green horizontal bands.
A seven-coloured square patchwork flag is co-official alongside it.
Its yellow represents mineral wealth in a landlocked Andean country.
